# Jubilees Chapter 16 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 16:6 — God's reasoning for revealing Sodom's fate to Abraham

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "Shall I hide from Abraham what I do, seeing that I know he will command his children..." | Archaic "seeing that" |
| LOGOS | "Shall I hide from Abraham what I am about to do, since I know that he will command his children..." | "Since" — formal |
| PNEUMA | "Should I hide from Abraham what I'm about to do? I know he will raise his children..." | Question then statement |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. "Since I know" preserves the causal-conditional structure of God's reasoning. PNEUMA's break into two sentences disrupts the logic of the rhetorical question. EMET's "seeing that" is archaic.

---

## 16:9 — Abraham's intercession: "Far be it from thee"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "Far be it from thee to do such a thing" | Archaic KJV phrasing |
| LOGOS | "Far be it from you to do such a thing" | Same, modernized |
| PNEUMA | "You couldn't possibly do that" | Colloquial rendering |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. "Far be it from you" is the established rendering of the Hebrew/Ge'ez imprecatory formula (chalilah lekha). PNEUMA's "you couldn't possibly" loses the legal/moral horror that the formula expresses.

---

## 16:18 — "that we may know them" vs. "we want to have sex with them"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "that we may know them" | Biblical euphemism preserved |
| LOGOS | "that we may know them" | Same — preserves the biblical idiom |
| PNEUMA | "We want to have sex with them" | Renders the euphemism explicitly |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. "Know them" is the established biblical euphemism (yada') preserved in translation tradition for this passage. PNEUMA's explicit rendering is accurate but overrides a deliberate stylistic choice of the source idiom.

---

## 16:22 — The blinding of the Sodomites

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "they smote the men who were at the door of the house with blindness, both small and great" | Literal "small and great" |
| LOGOS | "They struck the men at the door with blindness — great and small alike" | Same, inverted order |
| PNEUMA | "they struck every man at the door with blindness — young and old alike" | "Young and old" for "small and great" |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. "Great and small" is the Ge'ez merism preserving the Genesis idiom (Gen 19:11). PNEUMA's "young and old" interprets "small/great" as age rather than rank/status — a defensible but interpretive choice.

---

## 16:31 — Feast of Tabernacles ordained in Abraham's time

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "in this jubilee Abraham and Isaac and Jacob and all who were born of them were given the feast of Tabernacles as an everlasting ordinance" | Full literal |
| LOGOS | "In this jubilee, Abraham and Isaac and Jacob and all their descendants were given the Feast of Tabernacles as an everlasting ordinance" | Slight condensation |
| PNEUMA | "In this jubilee, the Feast of Tabernacles was established as an everlasting ordinance for Abraham and Isaac and Jacob and all their descendants" | Restructured passive |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. "Were given the Feast of Tabernacles" preserves the divine-gift framing. PNEUMA's passive "was established" is accurate but loses the recipient-gift structure.

---

**Total disagreements: 5**
